mainTopic: יומא 6b: When a בועל נדה immerses, why the כהן גדול is not guarded from טומאת מת, and whether טומאת מת is הותרה or דחויה בציבור
overview: This amud first finishes the challenge against רב שימי מנהרדעא, who held that a בועל נדה immerses at night. The גמרא tries to prove from a ברייתא that he immerses by day like a טמא מת, but that proof is pushed off. Then a ברייתא of רבי חייא says it outright, and רב שימי is refuted (תיובתא). Next the גמרא asks why the כהן גדול is kept away from his wife's impurity but not guarded from the more severe טומאת מת. רב תחליפא in the name of רבא answers that טומאת מת is permitted for communal service (הותרה בציבור). רבינא answers instead that טומאת מת is rare, while impurity from home is common. The גמרא then brings the מחלוקת of רב נחמן (הותרה) and רב ששת (דחויה), and shows the practical difference: must we bring pure כהנים from another בית אב? A second version (איכא דאמרי) says רב נחמן lets impure כהנים serve even beside pure ones in the same בית אב, and this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: So the comparison must be about immersion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that the ברייתא comparing a בועל נדה to a טמא מת must be teaching that both immerse during the day. That would contradict רב שימי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it that the comparison is about their immersion?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge against רב שימי. Since comparing a בועל נדה to a טמא מת can't be about how long their impurity lasts (the פסוק already says that), it must be about when they immerse: by day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the גמרא pointed out that the seven days of impurity for a בועל נדה are written openly in the תורה, so the ברייתא would add nothing by teaching them. That leaves immersion as the point of the comparison. A טמא מת immerses by day, so a בועל נדה would too, which goes against רב שימי's view that he immerses at night.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it that...? (the only remaining option)
Immersion in a מקוה
A man who had relations with a נדה; he is impure for seven days
A person made impure by a corpse

phrases.english: Rather, is it not regarding their immersion?
phrases.notes: The ברייתא compared בועל נדה to טמא מת; the גמרא suggests what they share is immersing during the day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the attempted proof against רב שימי that began on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שימי מנהרדעא's view that a בועל נדה immerses at night
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Comparing him to a טמא מת can't be about how long the impurity lasts, since the פסוק already says that. So it must be about immersion, which for a טמא מת is by day.

steps.title: The comparison is about impurity, needed for the later clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The comparison really is about the length of the impurity. The ברייתא included it only to set up its next clause, which shows how a בועל נדה is more severe than a טמא מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really it is about their impurity. The ברייתא needed it for the next clause: 'However, a בועל נדה is more severe than him, because he makes a bed or seat impure with a light impurity, enough to make foods and liquids impure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof. The comparison is about the seven-day impurity after all. It was written only so the ברייתא could go on to teach how the two cases differ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the claim that a comparison about the impurity would be pointless. The answer is that it was a lead-in: first the ברייתא says they are alike, then it shows the difference. A בועל נדה makes a bed or seat impure just by lying or sitting on it (מדרס), which a טמא מת does not. This is only a light impurity (ראשון לטומאה) that affects food and drink.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / truly (keeping the original reading)
He needed it for the later clause
Something one lies on or sits on
A light impurity (first degree) that only makes food and drink impure
Foods and liquids

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the בועל נדה makes the bed a full אב הטומאה like a זב does. The bed gets only a light impurity, strong enough only for food and drink, not for people or vessels.

phrases.english: No, actually it refers to their impurity,
he needed it for the latter clause:
However, one who had relations with a menstruating woman is more severe than him,
in that he makes a bed and a seat impure
phrases.notes: Just by lying or sitting on it, without touching.

phrases.english: with a light impurity,
enough to make foods and liquids impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְעוֹלָם לְטוּמְאָתָן, סֵיפָא אִצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge made in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. רב שימי's view is not refuted here. Steps 3-4 refute it with רבי חייא's ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that a comparison about impurity would teach nothing. In fact it sets up the next clause about how the two cases differ.

steps.title: רבי חייא's ברייתא: a בועל נדה immerses by day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא of רבי חייא that says plainly that a בועל נדה immerses by day, while a נדה and a יולדת immerse at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what רבי חייא taught: A זב, a זבה, a male and female מצורע, a בועל נדה, and a טמא מת immerse during the day. A נדה and a יולדת immerse at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new and clearer source against רב שימי. This ברייתא lists the בועל נדה among those who immerse by day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier ברייתא, this one doesn't depend on figuring out what a comparison means. It names the בועל נדה directly in the daytime group and keeps nighttime immersion only for a נדה and a יולדת. So the בועל נדה is not treated like the נדה herself.

keyTerms.meaning: A man or woman with an impure flow
A male or female with צרעת
A woman after childbirth
At night

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rabbi Chiyya taught:
The zav, the zavah, the male leper and the female leper,
and one who had relations with a menstruating woman, and one impure from a corpse,
their immersion is during the day;
a menstruating woman and a woman after childbirth, their immersion is at night!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was pushed off, a clearer source is brought.
steps.raayaObject: That a בועל נדה immerses during the day, against רב שימי
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא taught by רבי חייא

steps.title: רב שימי is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי חייא's ברייתא fully refutes רב שימי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא announces that רב שימי's view has been disproven and is not accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תיובתא means a later אמורא's view clashes with a תנאי source and has no way out. Here the conclusion is that a בועל נדה immerses by day.

keyTerms.meaning: A full refutation; the view is rejected

steps.whatToRemember: A בועל נדה immerses by day, like a טמא מת. Only a נדה and a יולדת immerse at night. רב שימי's opposing view is rejected.

phrases.english: A refutation.
phrases.notes: That one word settles it: the argument is knocked down and the discussion ends.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the result of the proof in step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב שימי is refuted; a בועל נדה immerses during the day.

steps.title: Why not also guard the כהן גדול from corpse impurity?
steps.stepSummary: Going back to the separation of the כהן גדול, the גמרא asks why the חכמים worried about impurity from his home but did not guard him from the more serious טומאת מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Before you separate him from the impurity of his house, separate him from the impurity of a corpse!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the seven-day separation of the כהן גדול. If the goal is to keep him pure, why not also protect him from טומאת מת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is kept away from his wife so he won't become a בועל נדה, which carries seven days of impurity. But טומאת מת also lasts seven days and is more severe, for example if someone died in his room. If we guard against the lighter impurity, we should surely guard against the more severe one.

keyTerms.meaning: Before you do this... (you should first do that)
You separate him
The impurity of his house, meaning from his wife
Impurity from a corpse

phrases.english: And before you separate him from the impurity of his house,
separate him from the impurity of a corpse!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the immersion topic and returns to the main subject: the separation of the כהן גדול.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the כהן גדול is separated from his house to keep him pure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If you guard against the lighter impurity of a בועל נדה, you should surely also guard against the more serious טומאת מת.

steps.title: Corpse impurity is permitted for communal service
steps.stepSummary: רב תחליפא, in the name of רבא, answers that טומאת מת is permitted when the service is communal. So it would not stop the יום כפור service, and there was no need to guard against it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב תחליפא, father of רב הונא בר תחליפא, said in the name of רבא: This shows that טומאת מת is permitted in communal service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. There is no need to guard the כהן גדול from טומאת מת, because communal offerings may be brought even in that state.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of טומאה הותרה בציבור means that when the whole community needs an offering and the כהנים are impure from a corpse, the service still goes on. The יום כפור service is communal, so טומאת מת would not stop it. The impurity of a בועל נדה is not covered by this permission, so that risk still needs guarding against.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches us (a principle learned from the case)
Was permitted
For the community / communal offerings
In the name of

steps.whatToRemember: טומאת מת הותרה בציבור: communal service such as יום כפור may be done even with טומאת מת. That is why the חכמים guarded the כהן גדול only from the impurity of his house.
steps.confusionAlert: This permission covers טומאת מת, not every kind of impurity. That is why becoming a בועל נדה is still a real concern.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a major principle (טומאה הותרה בציבור) that shapes how the גמרא understands the purpose of the כהן גדול's separation.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב תַּחְלִיפָא אֲבוּהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: Rav Tachlifa, father of Rav Huna, said
(bar Tachlifa) in the name of Rava:
That is to say:
impurity of a corpse is permitted in communal matters.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב תַּחְלִיפָא אֲבוּהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a legal principle that removes the concern
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any impurity would stop the כהן גדול's service, so he should be guarded from all of them, especially טומאת מת.
steps.terutzMaskana: טומאת מת does not stop communal service, so it needs no guarding. Only the impurity of a בועל נדה, which is not permitted, needs to be prevented.

steps.title: רבינא: corpse impurity is rare, impurity at home is common
steps.stepSummary: רבינא gives a different answer to the קשיא from step 5. Even if טומאת מת is only דחויה בציבור, it rarely happens, so there was no need to guard against it. Impurity from the כהן גדול's home happens often.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: You can even say that טומאת מת is only 'pushed aside' for the community. Still, טומאת מת is rare, while impurity from his house is common.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the same question that רב תחליפא answered in step 6, but in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב תחליפא said that טומאת מת would not stop the service, because it is fully permitted for the community. רבינא does not need that idea. He says the reason is practical: it is unlikely that someone visiting the כהן גדול will suddenly die, but a doubt about his wife becoming a נדה can come up at any moment. The חכמים made a safeguard only for the common risk.

keyTerms.meaning: Pushed aside: the rule still exists, but it gives way when there is a need
In a communal setting, such as a communal קרבן
Common, something that happens often
Impurity coming from his home, meaning from his wife

steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is not saying that טומאת מת is less serious. He is saying it is less likely to happen, so the חכמים did not make a special protection against it.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Even if you say that corpse impurity
is only overridden for the public,
corpse impurity is not common,
phrases.notes: It is unlikely that a visitor will suddenly die in his presence.

phrases.english: but impurity from his house is common.
phrases.notes: A doubt about his wife's נדה status can arise at any time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the step 5 question, which does not depend on step 6's claim that טומאת מת is הותרה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical likelihood, not the legal status of the impurity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since טומאת מת is more serious, it should have been guarded against even more.
steps.terutzMaskana: A safeguard is needed only for a common risk. טומאת מת is rare, but impurity from home is common.

steps.title: רב נחמן and רב ששת argue about corpse impurity in communal service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a מחלוקת. רב נחמן holds that טומאת מת is הותרה בציבור, fully permitted. רב ששת holds it is only דחויה בציבור, pushed aside.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated about טומאת מת: רב נחמן said it is permitted for the community. רב ששת said it is only pushed aside for the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an argument between אמוראים about the exact question that steps 6 and 7 touched on. This sets up the next steps, which will explain when they actually disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הותרה' means that when the community is impure, the service is treated as if there were no impurity at all. 'דחויה' means the prohibition still exists and only gives way when there is no choice, so a pure כהן is still preferred. Steps 9-10 explain what practical difference this makes.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted: the prohibition is fully removed in this setting
Impurity contracted from a dead body

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree that impure כהנים may serve for the community. The only question is whether the prohibition disappears completely, or is only set aside when needed.

phrases.english: It was stated: regarding corpse impurity,

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: הוּתְּרָה הִיא בְּצִיבּוּר,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: it is permitted for the public,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: דְּחוּיָה הִיא בְּצִיבּוּר.
phrases.english: and Rav Sheshet said: it is overridden for the public.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the full source for the two positions (הותרה and דחויה) mentioned in steps 6 and 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן: טומאת מת is הותרה בציבור. רב ששת: it is דחויה בציבור.

steps.title: Defining exactly where the two opinions disagree
steps.stepSummary: If one בית אב has both pure and impure כהנים, everyone agrees that only the pure ones serve. The argument is only about whether we must bring pure כהנים from a different בית אב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where there are impure and pure כהנים in that בית אב, everyone agrees that the pure ones serve and the impure ones do not. They disagree about whether to go and bring pure כהנים from another בית אב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the מחלוקת so we know its exact case. This prepares for the next step, which gives each side's ruling in that case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even רב נחמן agrees that pure כהנים who are already on duty come first. The real question is the case where the whole בית אב on duty that day is impure. Must we go and find pure כהנים from another family in the same משמר?

keyTerms.meaning: A family group of כהנים assigned to serve on one day of the week
Everyone agrees
To go seek out, to search for

phrases.english: Where there are impure and pure priests
in that patrilineal family,
everyone agrees
that the pure ones serve and the impure ones do not serve.
Where they disagree is whether to seek out
and bring pure priests from another patrilineal family.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the מחלוקת of step 8 to one specific case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Within one בית אב, pure כהנים serve first according to everyone. The מחלוקת is only about bringing כהנים from another בית אב.

steps.title: The practical outcome: do we search for pure priests elsewhere?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן: since טומאת מת is הותרה, we do not search for other כהנים. רב ששת: since it is only דחויה, we do search for pure כהנים from another בית אב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: it is permitted for the community, so we do not search. רב ששת said: it is only pushed aside for the community, so we do search.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats each opinion, now paired with its practical ruling in the case defined in step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows how the idea becomes a practical rule. If the prohibition is gone (הותרה), there is nothing to avoid, so the impure בית אב serves. If it is only set aside (דחויה), we must avoid it whenever we can, so we bring pure כהנים from elsewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: Permission: a complete allowance
We seek out, we go and search

steps.whatToRemember: הותרה means the prohibition is gone, so we do not search for pure כהנים (רב נחמן). דחויה means the prohibition is only set aside, so we search for pure כהנים from another בית אב (רב ששת). Within the same בית אב, everyone agrees that pure כהנים serve first.
steps.whyThisMatters: The pair הותרה / דחויה is a basic concept that comes up across ש״ס. This סוגיא gives its clearest practical test: do you have to work to avoid the prohibited situation?

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: הֶיתֵּר הִיא בְּצִיבּוּר,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: it is permitted for the public,
and we do not seek out other priests.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: דְּחוּיָה הִיא בְּצִיבּוּר,
phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet said: it is overridden for the public,
and we do seek out pure priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: הֶיתֵּר הִיא בְּצִיבּוּר, וְלָא מַהְדְּרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies each position from step 8 to the specific case defined in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן: we do not search for pure כהנים from another בית אב. רב ששת: we do search for them.

steps.title: Second version: רב נחמן lets impure כהנים serve even when pure ones are present
steps.stepSummary: In the איכא דאמרי version, רב נחמן argues even when one בית אב has both pure and impure כהנים. He says the impure ones may also serve.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: even where there are pure and impure כהנים in that same בית אב, רב נחמן disagrees, and says: the impure ones may also serve.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the רב נחמן and רב ששת argument. In this version, רב נחמן allows impure כהנים to serve even when pure כהנים from the same family are there. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (step 9), everyone agreed that if a בית אב has pure כהנים, only they serve. The argument there was only about bringing pure כהנים from another family. This new version moves the argument further: רב נחמן holds that טומאת מת is so fully הותרה בציבור that impure כהנים serve side by side with the pure ones.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritually pure (כהנים)
Ritually impure (כהנים)
He disagrees
They serve (do the עבודה)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In the first version, everyone agrees that pure כהנים in the same בית אב come first. In this איכא דאמרי version, רב נחמן disagrees even about that case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how far the idea of הותרה can go. If טומאה is truly permitted in a communal setting, then being impure is not even second-best. It is fully allowed.

phrases.english: Some say:
phrases.notes: This opens a second version of the מחלוקת from steps 8-10.

phrases.english: Even where there are pure and impure (כהנים)
in that same family group (on duty)
phrases.notes: This is the exact case where, in the first version, everyone agreed.

phrases.english: רב נחמן disagrees,
and says: the impure ones also serve,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud, where the reason is given.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אֲפִילּוּ הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא טְהוֹרִין וּטְמֵאִין בְּהָהוּא בֵּית אָב פְּלִיג רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the מחלוקת from steps 9-10. It makes the argument wider, so that it also covers the case where pure and impure כהנים are in the same בית אב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the איכא דאמרי, רב נחמן holds that impure כהנים may serve even when pure כהנים from the same בית אב are present.
